title: Code Quality
description: Review of the coding standard, compiler warnings, static analysis, code review practice, and maintainability.

items.text: A coding standard is chosen and enforced (e.g. MISRA C, CERT C, Barr Group)
items.hint: Record deviations with a reason, rather than switching rules off globally.

items.text: The build is warning-free with a strict warning set, and warnings fail CI
Static analysis runs in CI, and findings are triaged
items.hint: cppcheck, clang-tidy, or a commercial tool. Keep a reviewed baseline so new findings stand out.
So code review is about behavior, not whitespace.

items.text: MISRA compliance is reported with a deviation record where the client or standard asks for it
items.hint: Usually required for safety and automotive work.

items.text: Every change to the main branch is reviewed by a second engineer
items.hint: Use pull requests with required review.

items.text: Functions are small and their complexity is measured
items.hint: Flag cyclomatic complexity above about 15 for review.

items.text: Magic numbers are named, and units are clear in names or types
items.hint: timeout_ms, temp_c_x10. Unit mix-ups cause real bugs.

items.text: Comments explain why, and public interfaces are documented
items.hint: Header comments on each module's API, generated docs if useful.

items.text: Dead code and commented-out code are removed
Integer overflow, sign conversion, and undefined behavior are reviewed in arithmetic
items.hint: Especially in time calculations, scaling, and buffer index math.
